result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_graph_name()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the name of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3826-L3863){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_graph_name() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns the human-readable name assigned to this graph, if any. The name is an optional identifier that can be set when creating the graph or updated later. It's useful for distinguishing between multiple graphs in analysis or visualization contexts. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph's name if set, or None if no name was assigned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Get graph name: ::: {#646e6f3c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(graph_name="Social Network") # Returns "Social Network" graph.get_graph_name() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 'Social Network' ``` ::: ::: Handle graphs without names: ::: {#8c4fd12b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() name = graph.get_graph_name() # Returns None name ``` :::
